summary:
EthioCrop Advisor is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform developed by Team Qedamawiyan for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps Ethiopian farmers, agronomists, and development agents explore crop-rotation options using NASA Earth-observation data, farm-specific information, and local agro-ecological principles.

Users enter their farm location, soil type, current and previous crops, farm size, irrigation availability, and farming priorities. The platform combines this information with NASA POWER climate data and NASA GIBS satellite imagery, supported by Open-Meteo weather services and OpenStreetMap. A transparent, rule-based engine evaluates possible three-year cereal-legume rotations and presents three options with scores and explanations.

 Our goal is to make space-based environmental information more accessible and useful for agricultural planning in Ethiopia.
details:
EthioCrop Advisor is a web-based agricultural decision-support application designed to help Ethiopian farmers explore suitable crop-rotation possibilities for their farms and upcoming growing seasons. The project addresses the challenge of deciding what to plant after harvesting, considering factors such as changing weather conditions, rainfall, soil characteristics, water availability, previous crops, and farmers' priorities.

The platform works through four main stages. First, users select an Ethiopian location through a search function or interactive map and provide farm information, including soil type, current and previous crops, farm size, irrigation availability, and their main farming priority. Second, the system retrieves environmental information using NASA POWER Daily and Monthly APIs and displays NASA GIBS satellite imagery. Open-Meteo provides location search and a seven-day weather forecast, while OpenStreetMap provides the base map. Third, our transparent, rule-based rotation engine evaluates valid three-year cereal-legume crop sequences using temperature conditions, soil and water suitability, crop diversity, nitrogen fixation principles, and crop history. Finally, the platform presents three ranked options: Best Fit, Balanced, and Water-Saving, each with a score out of 100 and an explanation of the agronomic reasoning.

The project was developed using React with JSX components for the web interface and Node.js for the server-side processing and API services. It integrates NASA POWER Daily, NASA POWER Monthly, and NASA GIBS, alongside Open-Meteo Geocoding, Open-Meteo Weather Forecast, and OpenStreetMap services.

Our project is creative because it does more than display satellite and weather information. It connects environmental data with farm-specific information and an explainable agricultural decision-support model. We also designed the platform specifically around Ethiopian agricultural conditions, including Kolla and Dega agro-climatic zones, Kiremt, Belg, and Bega seasons, and locally relevant crops.

The platform is free to access, does not require an account, and supports English, Amharic, Afaan Oromoo, and Somali. Its intended benefits include helping users explore crop diversity, consider soil-health and water-conservation priorities, and understand how environmental conditions relate to crop-rotation decisions.

EthioCrop Advisor is currently a working prototype. Its rotation rules and scoring parameters still require review by Ethiopian agronomists and agricultural experts, followed by farmer feedback and field testing. We do not claim proven improvements in crop yield, income, or soil health. Our long-term vision is to validate the system, expand its crop and regional coverage, and investigate additional NASA datasets such as SMAP soil-moisture data and GPM IMERG rainfall products.
